verses.1: Give thanks to the LORD. Call upon his name. Make known among the nations his acts.
verses.2: Sing to him, make music to him. Tell of all his wondrous deeds.
verses.3: Glorify his holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
verses.4: Seek the LORD and his strength. Seek his presence continually.
verses.5: Remember the wonders he has done, the miracles and the judgments of his mouth.
verses.6: Descendants of Abraham his servant, sons of Jacob his chosen ones.
verses.7: He is the LORD our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
verses.8: He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations.
verses.9: The covenant he made with Abraham, and the oath he swore to Isaac.
verses.10: He established it as a decree for Jacob, as an eternal covenant for Israel.
verses.11: Saying, "I will give you the land of Canaan, the portion of your inheritance."
verses.12: When they were few in number, few and strangers in the land.
verses.13: They moved from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people.
verses.14: He did not allow anyone to mistreat them; he rebuked kings on their behalf.
verses.15: Do not harm my anointed ones; do not touch my prophets.
verses.16: He called a famine upon the land; the whole bread supply was broken.
verses.17: He sent a man before them, Joseph who was sold as a slave.
verses.18: They afflicted his feet with shackles, his soul went through fire, his life into exile.
verses.19: Until the time of his word came, the word of the LORD refined him.
verses.20: The king sent and released him, the ruler of nations and freed him.
verses.21: He set him over his house, master of all his possessions.
verses.22: To instruct his officials as he pleased, and to teach his elders wisdom.
verses.23: Then Israel came into Egypt, and Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
verses.24: He greatly increased his people, made them stronger than their enemies.
verses.25: He turned their hearts to hate his people, to act deceitfully toward his servants.
verses.26: He sent Moses his servant and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
verses.27: He gave them signs and miracles in the land of Ham.
verses.28: He sent darkness, and it grew dark, but they did not rebel against his word.
verses.29: He turned their waters into blood, and the fish died.
verses.30: Swarms of frogs rose up in the land, in the chambers of their kings.
verses.31: He spoke, and came flies and gnats into all their borders.
verses.32: He gave their rains as hail, fire flashing in their land.
verses.33: He struck their vines and their fig trees, shattered the trees of their borders.
verses.34: He spoke, and came locusts and grasshoppers, without number.
verses.35: They ate up all the grass in their land, all the fruit of their soil.
verses.36: He struck all their firstborn, the first of all their livestock.
verses.37: He brought them out with silver and gold, with no weak among his tribes.
verses.38: Egypt was glad when they went, for fear had fallen upon them.
verses.39: He spread a cloud for a canopy, and fire to light the night.
verses.40: He asked, and brought quail, and filled them with bread from heaven.
verses.41: He split a rock, and water flowed out, rivers ran in the desert.
verses.42: For he remembered his holy word, his promise to Abraham his servant.
verses.43: And he brought his people out with joy, his chosen ones with gladness.
verses.44: He gave them the lands of nations, and the toil of peoples they inherited.
verses.45: So that they might keep his statutes, and observe his teachings. Praise the LORD!

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: "Joseph who was sold as a slave" — the Hebrew uses "נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵֽף" which is literally "Joseph was sold."
- v. 18: "his soul went through fire" — "בַּרְזֶל בָּאָה נַפְשֽׁוֹ" is metaphorically rendered to reflect the ordeal.
- v. 19: "the word of the LORD refined him" — the metaphor of fire and refinement is implied by the context.
- v. 22: "to teach his elders wisdom" — "יְחַכֵּֽם" is best rendered as "to teach wisdom."
- v. 44: "and the toil of peoples they inherited" — the Hebrew "עֲמַל לְאֻמִּים" is interpreted as the labor or toil of other nations.
- v. 45: "Praise the LORD" — the Hebrew "הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ" is a poetic form of "Praise the LORD."
